results.title: Roger Federer turns 45: Achievements, family and a new chapter
results.content: Roger Federer turns 45 this Saturday, August 8, firmly established as one of the most beloved and respected figures in sports history. Four years after retiring, the Swiss icon remains a global role model, a leading ambassador for tennis, and a symbol of grace both on and off the court. These days, his life revolves around tribute events, occasional exhibition matches, personal ventures, appearances at the sport's biggest tournaments, and, above all, his family, the foundation of everything he [...] Roger Federer says raising his four children has become his greatest priority since retiring from professional tennis. [...] Federer retired with a résumé that remains one of the most remarkable in tennis history. He captured 20 Grand Slam singles titles, including a record eight Wimbledon championships, six Australian Opens, five U.S. Opens, and one French Open. Between 2001 and 2019, he won 103 career titles, second only to Jimmy Connors, and spent 310 weeks as the world's No. 1, including a record streak of 237 consecutive weeks.
